The results topped Wall Street expectations. The average estimate of four analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was breakeven on a per-share basis.

The business process management software provider posted revenue of $203.3 million in the period, also beating Street forecasts. Three analysts surveyed by Zacks expected $192.9 million.

🚨 Supply Chain Alert: Analog Devices (ADI) Announces Portfolio-Wide Price Adjustment Effective Sept 13, 2026
Analog Devices (ADI) has officially announced a company-wide price adjustment taking effect on September 13, 2026.
The move reflects continuous broad-based demand growth across industrial & automotive markets, alongside rising manufacturing, wafer fab, and packaging costs.
Key Takeaways for Procurement & Hardware Engineering Teams:
⏳ Action Window: Only a few weeks left before the September 13 deadline to review active BOMs and lock in critical component allocations.
📦 Buffer Planning: High-reliability industrial systems need proactive supply chain planning to prevent lead-time extensions or unexpected cost increases.
🔄 Second-Source Strategy: A great reminder of the importance of maintaining robust, pin-to-pin drop-in alternatives across all active & memory subsystems.

📈 The chip price hike wave is gaining steam in 2H26. After Texas Instruments raised prices in July, Analog Devices is reportedly gearing up for its second 2026 increase, set to take effect in mid-September.

🔥 Unlike its inflation-driven hike earlier this year, ADI reportedly says it will funnel all incremental revenue from the latest increases into wafer fab, packaging and testing capacity—aiming to cut lead times of up to six months.
